summary: Manager lookup timeout blocks access-request approval flow (HRIS -> Okta automation)
description:
Issue summary:
The Access Requests portal stalls when creating new role requests that require manager approval. The approval workflow queries the HRIS (Workday) for manager information; that lookup intermittently times out and leaves requests in the 'Needs Approval' state with no approver assigned.

Impact:
- Internal employees requesting temporary elevated console roles are blocked from receiving approvals.
- Oncall rotations and breakglass flows impacted for ~8% of requests since 2026-03-09 09:00 UTC.
- Operational friction for SRE and Platform teams; manual approvals required.

Environment:
- Access Requests v2 (internal portal) talking to HRIS proxy service -> Workday API and Okta automations.
- Observed in prod-us-east; staging not affected.

Current behavior:
- Request enters 'Needs Approval' and remains pending.
- Access Requests logs show manager_lookup timeout (500ms -> 3s) followed by a 504 from HRIS-proxy.
- Okta automation receives empty approver field and skips auto-assign.

Expected behavior:
- Manager lookup should return manager DN within configured SLA (500ms) or Access Requests should fallback to department-approver policy and alert on long latency.

Relevant logs & links:
- Access Requests trace IDs: trace-20260310-8a7c, trace-20260310-9bbf
- HRIS-proxy logs (filtered): https://grafana.redwood-internal.com/d/HRIS/logs?query=trace-20260310-8a7c
- Slack thread: #identity-ops (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234567)
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Login to Access Requests portal in prod-us-east.
2) Submit a role elevation request that requires manager approval for a user whose manager was recently changed in Workday.
3) Observe request transitions to 'Needs Approval' and no approver is assigned after 10 minutes.
4) Check access-requests service logs for manager_lookup timeout entries.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:45 UTC - Aisha Patel: Initial triage - reproduced with user whose Workday managerId changed yesterday. HRIS-proxy returned 504 intermittently. Filed this ticket and pinged identity-oncall.
2026-03-10 10:12 UTC - Liam Chen: Confirmed access-requests does not implement fallback to department approver when manager query fails. Added instrumentation to log empty approver events.
2026-03-10 11:02 UTC - SRE (oncall): HRIS-proxy CPU spikes correlated with increased Workday API latency. Possible rate-limiting/backoff misconfiguration. See grafana panel hrismetrics-2026-03-10.

2026-03-11 02:20 UTC - Identity eng: Workday reported a partial outage between 08:50-09:30 UTC that caused elevated latencies for manager lookup endpoint. Root cause appears to be a degraded caching layer in HRIS-proxy (redis misses) after a rolling deploy.

2026-03-11 09:30 UTC - Platform eng: Implemented a temporary increased timeout (3s -> 7s) on HRIS-proxy outbound calls to reduce 504s; helped some flows but surfaced design gap: no fallback in access-requests service.
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): 'Putting this on identity-oncall. Manual approvals are being done for impacted teams; tracking impact for next 24h.'
Liam Chen (2026-03-10): 'Added verbose logs and a feature flag to enable department-fallback behavior in Access Requests service. Will test in staging.'

Maya Rodriguez - HRIS Team (2026-03-11): 'Workday incident postmortem indicates transient cache eviction during config rollout. We rolled back yesterday. We'll coordinate with Identity to add a secondary lookup cache.'
SRE Oncall (2026-03-11): 'Observed 12% request failure rate to manager endpoint between 08:45-09:40 UTC. Restarted hrise-proxy nodes to clear connection pools; errors reduced to <1%.'
next_steps:
1) Identity eng to deploy department-fallback feature behind feature flag in Access Requests (PR #421).
2) HRIS team to harden hris-proxy cache + add metrics for redis miss rate.
3) SRE to add alert on manager_lookup_5xx_rate > 1% and a runbook link for manual approve procedure.
4) After stabilizing, remove temporary increased timeout and confirm baseline SLA.
5) Follow-up postmortem scheduled 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC.
